Toulouse, France, 09 October 2026 - Avolon, a leading global aviation finance company, has placed a firm order for 110 Airbus aircraft, comprising 35 A330-900 and 75 A320neo Family aircraft. This incremental order takes Avolon’s total for the A330-900 to 114 aircraft and the A320 Family to some 650.
"We continue to see strong demand for new aircraft, and this order further strengthens our long-term delivery pipeline. This positions us to support our airline customers' fleet growth and replacement requirements well into the next decade. We expect demand for both the A330neo and A320neo to remain strong given the long-term growth trajectory of the aviation sector, and we are delighted to further expand our longstanding partnership with Airbus through this agreement,” said Andy Cronin, Avolon CEO.
“This is a major order for both the A330neo and the A320neo Family and we thank Avolon for its repeated endorsement of our products,” said Benoît de Saint-Exupéry, Airbus EVP Sales of the Commercial Aircraft business. “With this acquisition, Avolon confirms its position as the leading lessor for the A330-900, having purchased 114 of the type from Airbus. It is also another demonstration of the strong demand for the A330neo and A320neo from the lessor community, who clearly value the broad market appeal and flexibility these two products offer in the market space from domestic to regional to long haul routes.”
Powered by the latest generation Rolls-Royce Trent 7000 engines, the A330neo is designed to fly up to 8,100 nautical miles / 15,000 kilometers non-stop and reduces fuel burn, CO₂ emissions and operating cost by 25% compared to previous generation competitor aircraft. The A330neo unique Airspace cabin offers passengers and crews the latest modern in-flight products for a comfortable flying experience.
The A320 Family is the world’s most popular single-aisle aircraft, having won more than 20,400 orders globally. The Family includes the largest member, the A321neo , offering unparalleled range and performance. The Family offers at least 20% fuel savings and CO₂ reduction compared to previous generation single-aisle aircraft, while maximising passenger comfort with one of the widest single-aisle cabins in the sky.

Toulouse, France, 7 October 2026 – Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the national flag carrier of Bangladesh, has signed a firm order for 10 latest-generation Airbus aircraft. The order includes four A350-900 widebody and six A321neo single-aisle aircraft, marking a significant step in the airline's fleet modernisation strategy and its ambition to expand its international network.
Operating from its primary hub in Dhaka, the airline will leverage the latest-generation aircraft's exceptional range, efficiency and operating economics to strengthen its network. The aircraft will support Biman Bangladesh Airlines' plans to serve North America, along with key destinations across Europe and the Middle East.
Bangladesh is experiencing a significant demographic dividend that reinforces its medium-term economic trajectory. This economic momentum directly catalyses demand across the aviation industry. Additionally, a vast overseas diaspora, particularly across the Middle East and Southeast Asia, continues to maintain high baseline demand for international routes, while growing foreign trade will drive commercial air cargo needs that Airbus’ latest generation products are well placed to support.
“Bangladesh is a dynamic nation of 200 million people, backed by a resilient economy and a rapidly growing travel market. We are uniquely supported by a deeply connected global diaspora of 15 million people. In this context, our planned fleet expansion represents a measured and reasonable ambition,” said Rumee A. Hossain, Chairman, Board of Directors, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
"This order marks a significant milestone in our partnership with Biman Bangladesh Airlines, as it embarks on this important phase of fleet modernisation. Together, the A350 and A321neo form the perfect fleet strategy for Biman as it spreads its wings to new international destinations, catering to the growing demand across its network,” said Benoît de Saint-Exupéry, EVP Sales of the Airbus Commercial Aircraft business. “Airbus’s aircraft will provide the airline with the efficiency, range and versatility needed to connect Bangladesh to key markets across the globe, while delivering an exceptional experience to its passengers.”
The A350 is the world’s most modern widebody aircraft, designed to fly up to 9,700 nautical miles / 18,000 kilometres non-stop, setting new standards for intercontinental travel. The aircraft includes state-of-the-art technologies and aerodynamics delivering unmatched standards of efficiency and comfort. Its latest generation Rolls-Royce engines and use of lightweight materials bring a 25 per cent advantage in fuel burn, operating costs and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions, compared to previous generation competitor aircraft. The A350’s unique Airspace cabin offers passengers and crews the latest modern in-flight products for a comfortable flying experience.
The A321neo, the largest member of Airbus’ best-selling A320neo Family , offers segment-leading operating economics and extended range, enabling airlines to serve regional and medium-haul routes with greater flexibility. Compared with previous-generation aircraft, the A321neo delivers lower fuel consumption and CO₂ emissions of at least 20%.

Marignane, France, 7 October 2026 – The government of Romania has signed a contract for the procurement of 12 Airbus H225M helicopters. The agreement was concluded with the French Armament General Directorate (DGA) in the frame of the European Commission’s Security Action for Europe (SAFE). The European Union’s financial instrument is designed to provide financial support to Member States to speed up defence readiness by allowing urgent and major investments in support of the European defence industry, with a focus on closing critical capability gaps.
“We are honoured that Romania has chosen the H225M to strengthen its defence capabilities. This selection will also bolster Romania’s industrial capabilities through our long term partnership with IAR, Romania’s sole helicopter manufacturer,” said Matthieu Louvot, CEO of Airbus Helicopters. “We are proud to welcome Romania within the growing H225M community, establishing the H225M as a key asset of Europe’s defence,” he added.
Airbus has been present in Romania for over twenty years through its three businesses. Airbus Helicopters’ customer centre keeps proving to be a successful enterprise since its creation, providing support and services to the Romanian Airbus fleets while working for various export customers. Airbus Defence and Space provides turn-key secure communications and systems engineering services through its engineering department, whilst Airbus’ Commercial Aircraft business manufactures strategic parts.
The Romanian Air Force currently operates the IAR-330 Puma, a locally produced version of the Puma under an Aerospatiale license. The 12 H225Ms will initiate the replacement of the Puma fleet for conventional and special operations. Romania has also previously ordered two H215Ms in naval configuration.
This contract is the second one signed by Romania and Airbus Helicopters in the frame of the SAFE initiative, with seven H160 and five H145 recently ordered for public services missions.
The H225M has proven its reliability and durability in combat conditions and crisis areas around the world. There are more than 350 H225s and H225Ms in service, totalling more than one million flight hours. The twelve H225M customers include Brazil, France, Hungary, Indonesia, Iraq, Kuwait, Malaysia, Mexico, Morocco, the Netherlands, Singapore, and Thailand.

Toulouse, France, 30 September 2026 – FLYONE Armenia, the country's largest carrier, has finalised an order with Airbus for the acquisition of two A321neo aircraft. The agreement was first announced as a Memorandum of Understanding during French President Emmanuel Macron’s official visit to Yerevan on the 5th May 2026.
The two A321neo aircraft, representing FLYONE Armenia’s first direct order from Airbus, will be powered by CFM International’s LEAP engines. Configured with a 239-seat all-economy layout, these aircraft are central to the carrier’s strategic fleet enhancement and represent a key milestone in its ambitious route network expansion. Established in 2021, the airline currently operates a fleet of 11 A320 Family aircraft.
“Our first direct order with Airbus marks an important and symbolic milestone in FLYONE Armenia’s development. Having two new A321neo aircraft built by Airbus specifically for our airline reflects our continued commitment to fleet modernisation and long-term growth. We are proud to strengthen our partnership with Airbus and are confident that this investment will support not only FLYONE Armenia’s future development, but also the continued growth of Armenia’s civil aviation sector and its international cooperation,” said Aram Khachatryan, CEO of FLYONE Armenia.
“This first direct order from FLYONE Armenia underscores the airline's commitment for operational excellence and enhanced passenger comfort as it continues to expand its A320 Family fleet,” said Benoît de Saint-Exupéry, Airbus EVP Sales of the Commercial Aircraft business. “We are very happy to welcome FLYONE as a new member of the Airbus family and we look forward to a deep and fruitful collaboration together to support their strategic growth plans.”
The A320 Family is the world’s most popular single-aisle aircraft, having won more than 20,000 orders globally. The Family includes the largest member, the A321neo, offering unparalleled range and performance. The Family offers at least 20% fuel savings and CO₂ reduction compared to previous generation single-aisle aircraft, while maximising passenger comfort with one of the widest single-aisle cabins in the sky.

Toulouse, France, 2 October 2026 – Dutch national carrier KLM, member of the Air France-KLM Group, has taken delivery of its first A350-900 . The milestone marks the introduction of the latest generation widebody for long-haul operations as part of the airline's ongoing fleet renewal. KLM currently operates an Airbus fleet of ten A330 Family aircraft and seventeen A321neos. The A350 will be operated on long-haul routes from its home base in Amsterdam Airport Schiphol to destinations like Toronto, strengthening the airline’s global network.
The newly delivered A350 for KLM seats 331 passengers in a three-class layout, featuring 34 Business Class suites with direct aisle access, 26 Premium Comfort seats, and 271 Economy seats. The aircraft is equipped with a comfortable and spacious Airspace cabin, designed to improve the long-haul experience for both passengers and crew through enhanced ergonomics and greater comfort, offering larger luggage capacity, advanced ambient lighting, and high-speed satellite connectivity.
The A350 is the world’s most modern widebody aircraft, designed to fly up to 9,700 nautical miles / 18,000 kilometres non-stop, setting new standards for intercontinental travel. The aircraft includes state-of-the-art technologies and aerodynamics delivering unmatched standards of efficiency and comfort. Its latest generation Rolls-Royce engines and use of lightweight materials bring a 25 per cent advantage in fuel burn, operating costs and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions, compared to previous generation competitor aircraft.
At the end of August 2026, the A350 Family had won over 1,620 orders from 69 customers worldwide.

Melbourne, Australia, 15 September 2026 – Melbourne-based logistics and supply chain enterprise, Linfox Group, has taken delivery of Australia’s first Airbus H160 helicopter, marking a landmark moment for next-generation rotorcraft in the region.
With this delivery, Linfox became the first operator in Australia to bring the twin-engine Airbus H160 into service. The state-of-the-art helicopter will support the business and corporate aviation requirements of the Linfox Group, operating across Australia’s diverse geography from urban hubs to regional destinations.
"Linfox has built its reputation over decades on the highest standards of safety, professionalism, and operational performance, and the H160 reflects exactly those principles," said Linfox founder, Lindsay Fox.
"Being the first to bring this aircraft into service in Australia is a proud moment for our team and a clear statement of our commitment to operating the most technologically advanced platform on the market."
The H160 is certified for up to 12 passengers. Linfox Aviation has selected an 8-passenger configuration, allowing guests to fully experience the aircraft’s expansive windows, airy cabin, and industry-leading technology.
"We are incredibly proud of this endorsement of the H160 by one of Australia’s most respected operators," said Olivier Michalon, Executive Vice President of Global Business at Airbus Helicopters. "The H160 joins their fleet as the world’s most technologically advanced medium twin-engine helicopter, exceptionally suited for Australia’s varied terrain," he added.
The aircraft was prepared for its entry into service locally by Pacific Crown Helicopters (PCH), a Part 145 certified maintenance organisation and long-standing Airbus Helicopters partner, ensuring support to the highest international airworthiness standards from day one.
The H160 is designed as a multi-role helicopter capable of performing a wide range of missions, including public services (such as search and rescue, homeland security, law enforcement, and emergency medical services), military operations, offshore transportation, and private and business aviation.
The aircraft is engineered to optimise performance and safety. Featuring the advanced Helionix avionics suite, the aircraft delivers highly intuitive flight controls, vastly improved situational awareness, and a significantly lightened workload for pilots.
Designed for diverse landscapes like Australia’s, the H160 Arrano engines deliver up to an 18% reduction in fuel burn compared to previous-generation engines in its class, and the aircraft is certified to operate on fuel blends containing up to 50% Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF).
Additionally, its curved Blue Edge main rotor blades reduce the aircraft's external acoustic footprint by up to 50% compared to previous generation helicopters.
Through continuous design improvements, the H160’s official empty weight has been reduced, providing operators with an increased payload of 100 kg or an additional 60 nm of range.
Today’s delivery ensures Australia joins an exclusive but rapidly growing global footprint of more than 70 H160 helicopters operating worldwide, which have already accumulated more than 14,000 flight hours in just the past year.

Ottobrunn / Taufkirchen, Germany, 12 October 2026 – Airbus, in partnership with Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), has successfully completed the first flight of the “U740-Valkyrie” in Europe. This key milestone confirms that Airbus and Kratos are on track to deliver a combat-ready uncrewed Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) by 2029, addressing the operational requirements of the German and other European Armed Forces.
Conducted at a test facility in Northern Europe, the flight achieved all objectives, including a runway independent rocket-assisted take-off, manoeuvers at various altitudes and speeds up to Mach 0.8, as well as in-flight mission adjustments. This debut paves the way for subsequent, more sophisticated flight tests with Airbus’ Multi-platform Autonomous Reconfigurable and Secure (MARS) mission system. Serving as the aircraft’s “European brain” and ensuring full control over software as well as mission applications, data and system hardware, MARS enables national German or European sovereignty from operational usage of the Valkyrie. MARS utilises AI-enhanced software to conduct missions autonomously and coordinate entire mission groups. A strict control hierarchy ensures a human remains on the loop, guaranteeing all critical decisions comply with established rules of engagement, as well as ethical and legal standards.
“In an increasingly complex and contested threat environment, air forces require affordable combat mass,” said Mike Schoellhorn, CEO of Airbus Defence and Space. “By pairing Kratos’ proven airframe as a ‘program of record’ with Airbus’ sovereign European mission system, we are able to offer a robust, sovereign, affordable, and combat-ready CCA system by the end of the decade. The Valkyrie will also play a critical role in enhancing crewed combat aircraft such as the Eurofighter with extended range, firepower, and survivability. The aircraft design enables operational resilience through its rail launch capability, while offering conventional, runway based, take-off and landing as an option.”
“First flights typically include plenty of learning opportunities, but with the maturity of the Valkyrie system and the well-integrated Airbus and Kratos team, this flight was an amazing success,” said Eric DeMarco, President and CEO of Kratos. “We’re proud to be partnering with Airbus on the CCA opportunities in Germany and other parts of the world. Combining the strengths of Kratos and Airbus enables the affordable Valkyrie system and Kratos’ CCA and drone manufacturing legacy to evolve with MARS and Airbus’ other high-capability subsystems, experience, and extensive knowledge across the full aerospace spectrum.”
About the U740 Valkyrie
With a length of 9.1m and a wingspan of 8.2m, the U740 Valkyrie features an internal weapons bay and external payload stations under the wings. It has a maximum take-off weight of approximately three tonnes, a range exceeding 5,000 kilometres, and a service ceiling of 45,000 feet. The U740 Valkyrie is engineered to operate autonomously or under the command of crewed fighters, such as the Eurofighter, to execute high-risk missions and protect crewed assets.

René Obermann to step down from the Board of Directors to focus on his SAP mandate
Amparo Moraleda to succeed René Obermann as Chair from 1 October, as previously announced
Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, co-opted to complete René Obermann’s remaining term; will seek a three-year mandate at the 2027 Annual General Meeting (AGM)
Florent Menegaux, CEO of Michelin, selected to succeed Jean-Pierre Clamadieu at the end of his planned mandate and to seek a three-year mandate at 2027 AGM
Amparo Moraleda and Oliver Zipse to seek renewed three-year mandates at 2027 AGM
Mark Dunkerley appointed as Chair of the Remuneration, Nomination and Governance Committee and Lead Independent Director
Amsterdam, the Netherlands, 1 October 2026 – Airbus SE (stock exchange symbol: AIR) announces key changes to its Board of Directors following its meeting held on 1 October 2026.
Following the announcement in April 2026 of his decision to step down, René Obermann will leave the Airbus Board of Directors effective 1 October 2026 to concentrate on his recent mandate as Non-Executive Director and incoming Chairman of the Supervisory Board at SAP.
To replace René Obermann as Non-Executive Director for the remainder of his term, the Board of Directors has co-opted Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML. He will subsequently seek a full three-year mandate at the next Annual General Meeting (AGM) in April 2027.
In addition, Jean-Pierre Clamadieu has informed the Board that he will not seek a new mandate at the 2027 AGM upon the expiration of his current term. Florent Menegaux, CEO of Michelin, has been selected to succeed Jean-Pierre Clamadieu and will seek a three-year mandate as a Non-Executive Director at the 2027 AGM.
Amparo Moraleda, who assumes her role as Chair of the Airbus Board of Directors on 1 October 2026, and Oliver Zipse, former Chairman of the Board of Management of BMW AG, whose terms expire at the next AGM, will both seek renewed mandates from shareholders at the 2027 AGM.
Additionally, the Board of Directors has designated Mark Dunkerley to serve as Chair of the Remuneration, Nomination and Governance Committee and Lead Independent Director, succeeding Amparo Moraleda in this capacity.
"On behalf of the entire Board, I want to express our deepest gratitude to René for his exemplary leadership and unwavering dedication as Chair over the past eight years,” said Amparo Moraleda, Chair of the Airbus Board of Directors. “As I step into this role, I look forward to working closely with my fellow Directors, drawing on their deep expertise to ensure Airbus remains agile, resilient, and well-positioned to seize future opportunities and navigate the challenges ahead."
"I would like to warmly thank René for his commitment, trusted partnership and rigorous focus on long-term value creation throughout his tenure as Chair,” said Guillaume Faury, Airbus CEO. “René provided steadfast guidance through many of the crises that Airbus navigated during his mandate, including the COVID pandemic. He consistently championed innovation in aerospace and defence, encouraging team Airbus to push boundaries across our businesses. I wish him the best in his future responsibilities and look forward to working closely with Amparo and the Board to continue driving Airbus’ long-term growth and strategic ambitions."

Paris, France, 10 September 2026 – Today, during the International Space Summit, in Paris, and in the presence of Philippe Baptiste, Minister of Higher Education, Research and Space for France, Eutelsat has ordered 229 more satellites from Airbus to strengthen its OneWeb constellation.
Eutelsat has signed an Authorisation to Proceed (ATP) with Airbus Defence and Space covering initial industrial activities for these 229 satellites. They are planned in addition to the 440 satellites already procured from Airbus due for delivery and launch soon. It will bring the total of new OneWeb satellites manufactured by Airbus to 669, and will ensure and enhance service continuity of the OneWeb constellation.
The satellites will be manufactured at Airbus Defence and Space’s Toulouse facility, already actively delivering the previous batches, enabling production continuity, rapid and homogeneous delivery rate.
Eutelsat’s OneWeb Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite network delivers high-speed, low-latency connectivity on a global basis. With over 600 satellites flying in 12 synchronised orbital planes 1,200km above the Earth, the constellation brings high-speed internet to every corner of the planet. The availability of these latest satellites will assure full operational continuity for customers of the constellation, progressively replacing early batches coming to the end of their operational life.
This new batch will encompass all features from the previous satellites and improvements gained throughout the programme development. Notably, advanced digital channelisers, for enhanced onboard processing capabilities, efficiency and flexibility, as well as the capacity to embark hosted payloads in addition to the OneWeb Ku mission.
“This is an exciting next step for OneWeb and for Eutelsat’s LEO strategy. With the first satellites from the 440 due for delivery and launch soon, our replenishment programme is moving forward. The planned addition of 229 more satellites will further strengthen OneWeb, while IRIS² will bring significant new capacity and capabilities. Together, they give us a powerful roadmap to serve our customers, grow our LEO business and reinforce our role at the heart of Europe’s sovereign connectivity future,” said Jean-François Fallacher, Eutelsat Chief Executive Officer.
“This new contract from Eutelsat highlights the maturity of our product, the excellence of our supply chain and their trust in our industrial know-how for high rate satellite manufacturing for large-scale LEO constellations. This is also a further step for European sovereignty, for which Airbus and Eutelsat have been key partners for decades!” said Alain Fauré, Head of Space Systems in Airbus Defence and Space.

Marignane, France, 10 September 2026 – The French Aeronautical Maintenance Directorate (DMAé) has placed an additional order with Airbus Helicopters following the successful evaluation of an initial U050 Capa-X system acquired at the end of 2025. This order covers the supply of four systems, each comprising two U050 Capa-X Uncrewed Aerial Systems (UAS), with two intended for the French Navy and two for the French Army as part of the Light Tactical Drone System (SDTL) evaluation programme. Delivery of the systems is scheduled for 2027.
"We are honoured that the DMAé has selected our U050 Capa-X drone to equip the French Navy and Army. This is a testament to their trust and a decisive milestone for the programme, which officially enters its operational phase," said Victor Gerin-Roze, Head of Uncrewed Aerial Systems at Airbus Helicopters. "This initial version of the U050 Capa-X is designed to evolve both in its design and the scope of its missions to adapt to the constantly changing needs of the armed forces. This is the core advantage of its modularity, which allows us to reinforce and expand its capabilities over time," he added.
Following a land and sea evaluation campaign conducted with various French forces in 2025 and early 2026, the U050 Capa-X successfully met the requirements of the SDTL programme. The system proved fully satisfactory, demonstrating a very small logistical footprint,with the complete setup fitting onto two pickup trucks,as well as a proven 7-hour endurance, dual-payload capacity, and an operational range of 100 km.
The U050 Capa-X is a 120 kg uncrewed aerial system capable of operating up to 100 km from its ground station via a direct data link. It offers up to 10 hours of endurance and a maximum payload capacity of 20 kg. As a modular drone, it can carry multiple payloads simultaneously and be rapidly configured to suit various missions.
In this initial configuration, it is equipped with an optronic pod dedicated to imagery intelligence (IMINT) for gathering and exploiting imagery for surveillance, reconnaissance, and operational analysis. It also integrates a signals intelligence (SIGINT) capability, enhancing its versatility in the field. This baseline architecture is designed to evolve, allowing for the integration of new capabilities based on operational requirements.
The Aeronautical Maintenance Directorate (DMAé) is a joint-service organisation reporting to the Chief of the Defence Staff. It is responsible for the performance and through-life support of aircraft and aeronautical equipment, ensuring asset availability while maintaining controlled costs.

Endorsed by EEHC, this agreement with UEEPC, MDEPC, and CEPC strengthens Egypt’s energy security through the modernization of five gas turbines, providing up to 1,250 MW of combined capacity.
Services solutions aim to extend the operating life of the equipment at the Kureimat, Nubaria, and Cairo North power plants by 13 to 15 years.
This collaboration underscores a commitment to long-term performance, fuel efficiency, and the continuous development of Egypt’s power infrastructure
CAIRO, EGYPT - (September 23, 2026) - GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE: GEV) announced today a services agreement to provide Rotor Life Extension (RLE) solutions for five GE Vernova 9F gas turbines at the Kureimat, Nubaria, and Cairo North power plants in Egypt. The agreement is with affiliates of the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company (EEHC) - Upper Egypt Electricity Production Company (UEEPC), Middle Delta Electricity Production Company (MDEPC), and Cairo Electricity Production Company (CEPC) - and was endorsed by EEHC.
Under the agreement, GE Vernova is expected to help extend the operating life of the five gas turbines - representing a total capacity of approximately 1,250 MW - by 13 to 15 years. The relevant services will be executed between 2028 and 2035.
The gas turbine rotor is a core component of the power plant that requires scheduled maintenance. This project supports the overall rotor lifecycle by utilizing GE Vernova’s expertise to determine the full residual life of components, aiming to ensure that they operate more efficiently and effectively.
This services agreement underscores the ongoing collaboration between GE Vernova, EEHC, and its generation company affiliates. By focusing on the long-term integrity of these important gas power assets, the initiative aims to bolster the reliability and efficiency of Egypt’s energy production.
“This agreement reflects EEHC’s continued focus on preserving the long-term performance and reliability of important generation assets across our fleet,” said Eng. Gaber El-Desouki, Chairman of the Board of Directors & CEO, Egyptian Electricity Holding Company (EEHC). “By working with GE Vernova and our generation companies, we are taking practical and proactive steps that can help protect strategic assets, support efficient and reliable power production, and contribute to Egypt’s broader electricity and energy objectives.”
“Extending the life of these gas turbines across our generation companies is expected to support grid stability and the continued availability of dispatchable power, while helping us increase the value of existing infrastructure and avoid premature, capital-intensive replacement,” said Eng. Mahmoud Al-Naqeeb, Full-time Board Member for Electricity Production Companies Affairs.
Egypt’s power sector is undergoing a significant transformation balancing the need to meet rapidly rising energy demand with an ambitious drive to enhance operational efficiency and integrate a growing share of renewable energy. Within this dynamic landscape, thermal power generation—primarily driven by combined-cycle gas turbines—continues to serve as the critical backbone of the nation's grid, currently accounting for approximately 80% of the country’s electricity production.
“As Egypt’s electricity needs continue to evolve, maintaining and modernizing existing gas power assets, such as those at Kureimat, Nubaria, and Cairo North, is essential to support reliability, improve fuel use, and strengthen energy system resilience,” said Joseph Anis , President & CEO, Europe, Middle East & Africa, GE Vernova’s Gas Power business . “This agreement reflects our continued commitment to working closely with EEHC, its affiliates, and other stakeholders in Egypt to support energy security through reliable and more efficient power generation. By helping extend the life of critical gas turbines, we aim to support our customers’ long-term operational priorities, optimize the value of existing infrastructure, and contribute to the continued development of Egypt’s power sector.”
The agreement builds on GE Vernova’s ongoing efforts to support the modernization and long-term performance of Egypt’s power generation fleet. In April 2026, GE Vernova announced an order from MDEPC to support modernization efforts at the Banha and Nubaria power plants , including Advanced Gas Path upgrades and multiyear services agreements. This initiative builds upon decades of cooperation with Egypt’s power sector, reinforcing GE Vernova's role in helping to meet the nation's evolving energy demands through advanced technology and lifecycle services.
For more than 50 years, GE Vernova’s businesses have supported Egypt’s electricity infrastructure through technologies and solutions, local talent development, and financing for projects across the power sector. Today, GE Vernova supports customers in Egypt across power generation, transmission, software, and services. GE Vernova’s installed base in Egypt includes more than 60 gas and steam turbines with a combined generating capacity of approximately 10 gigawatts.

(September 16, 2026) – Vineyard Wind and GE Vernova today announced that the parties have reached an amicable settlement to resolve all outstanding litigation regarding the Vineyard Wind offshore wind project. As part of this agreement, GE Vernova has withdrawn its notice of termination, and both parties have agreed to dismiss all pending legal claims.
The Vineyard Wind project is a key part of Massachusetts and New England’s plan to meet rising electricity demand. Today, all turbines are capable of producing power, providing reliable, affordable energy to more than 400,000 homes and businesses while bolstering grid stability across the Commonwealth. Beyond its energy contribution, the project is a significant economic engine, having created nearly 4,000 jobs and $1.94 billion in total economic output to date. Its environmental impact is equally substantial, cutting carbon emissions by more than 1.6 million metric tons annually—the equivalent of removing 325,000 cars from the road.
The terms of the settlement agreement are confidential.

Will build on robust 2026 effort to recruit and develop the next generation of energy innovators
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. – October 6, 2026 – GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) today announced its goal to double the number of MIT interns and permanent hires it brings on board in 2027, a meaningful expansion of its Alliance with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) that underscores GE Vernova’s commitment to building the workforce of the future. The announcement was made at the MIT x GE Vernova Alliance Fall Fair, held today at Hockfield Court on the MIT campus.
“Among the students on campuses today are the engineers, innovators and future leaders who will define the next era of energy, and our job is to give more of them the opportunity to join us, grow with us, and change the world,” said Scott Strazik , CEO of GE Vernova . "MIT is one of our most important partners in that effort, and what we're building together isn't incremental – we are doubling down. We are working together to identify the very best talent and enable them to make a real impact."
The event today brings together MIT students, faculty, and GE Vernova leaders and engineers to showcase the company's research collaborations, career opportunities, and technology innovation. This year's event features 12 Alliance Year Two research poster presentations, live technology demonstrations including robotics, large voltage monitoring detection, and frontal polymerization research, and a recruiting zone staffed to support interest in 2027 internship opportunities.
GE Vernova and MIT are in the second year of their Energy and Climate Alliance, a $50 million, five-year commitment spanning breakthrough research across the entire energy ecosystem: from generating electrons to moving them around the world efficiently. Beyond research, the Alliance is designed to develop the energy sector's future workforce through fellowships, internships, and a dedicated career exploration program connecting MIT students and faculty with opportunities across GE Vernova's global teams. In 2026 the company welcomed 80 MIT interns and permanent hires.
"The energy transition will require a generation of talent that is deeply technical, globally minded, and ready to solve problems at scale," said Steven Baert , Chief People Officer of GE Vernova . "Doubling our MIT intern and hiring numbers in a single year isn't something we're doing lightly, it's a signal of how seriously we take investing in talent early, and our commitment to building career pathways that give the best and brightest a place to do the most meaningful work of their careers."
GE Vernova recruits from a wide range of universities and engineering programs across the United States and globally as part of its broader talent and workforce development strategy.
Today's announcement reflects an urgent workforce reality outlined in GE Vernova's inaugural NextGen Workforce Study : the U.S. energy sector could need more than two million workers by 2032. To meet the massive growth in electricity demand driven by AI, data centers, and the industrial electrification surge, the study finds the industry will need one in every ten engineering graduates to join the power sector. GE Vernova's expanded MIT commitment is part of a broader effort to make those pathways visible and accessible earlier.
For more information about the GE Vernova and MIT Alliance, visit here . For more information about GE Vernova's Internship programs, visit here .

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) authorized the emergency exchange to alleviate supply disruption due to inclement weather in the Gulf of America
Energy.gov
October 10, 2026
Estimated Read Time min
WASHINGTON— The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the authorization of an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) to address supply disruptions due to inclement weather in the Gulf of America. Under the terms of the exchanges, participating companies will return the borrowed crude oil with additional premium barrels in 2027, helping replenish and strengthen the SPR at no additional cost to taxpayers. “With this emergency exchange, the Energy Department is acting swiftly to help maintain refinery operations, limit disruptions to fuel supplies, and ensure American families and businesses continue to have access to affordable, reliable, and secure energy” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright . “In addition to helping minimize supply disruptions, these emergency exchanges will also require Exxon and BP to return more barrels to the Reserve than are currently being withdrawn, saving taxpayers millions of dollars. Rest assured, the Trump Administration is committed to strengthening America’s energy security at every opportunity.” The Department has authorized exchanges of up to 2 million barrels each for ExxonMobil and BP America. ExxonMobil's exchange will accelerate deliveries of previously awarded SPR crude oil to address immediate supply needs. DOE will continue working with industry partners to support reliable fuel supplies and respond to hurricane-related disruptions. For more information about the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, visit energy.gov .

Secretary Wright issues an emergency order to stabilize the mid-Atlantic grid and mitigate the risk of blackouts
Energy.gov
October 12, 2026
Estimated Read Time min
WASHINGTON— U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright issued an emergency order to mitigate blackout risks in the mid-Atlantic ahead of a period of elevated demand, a high rate of planned generator outages during the autumn maintenance season, and numerous planned transmission outages. The order directs PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) to dispatch specified units and to order their operation as needed to maintain reliability and authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3. PJM is authorized to call upon its Transmission Owners and Electric Distribution Companies to implement the order as needed. The order was issued pursuant to an application from PJM submitted on October 11, 2026. “This order will help ensure millions of American families and businesses across the mid-Atlantic have access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity by making additional power generation, including backup power, available to use as needed,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright . “While past leaders’ energy subtraction policies have made the grid more vulnerable to the risk of blackouts when the sun doesn’t shine or the wind doesn’t blow, this administration remains committed to using every available tool to prevent blackouts.” DOE estimates more than 35 GW of unused backup generation remains available nationwide. The order is effective October 13, 2026, through October 16, 2026.

The Energy Department Announces Intention to Support Adding 2.5 GW of Grid Capacity and 800 Jobs
Energy.gov
October 13, 2026
Estimated Read Time min
WASHINGTON— The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced plans to lower electricity costs and strengthen grid reliability by supporting the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in funding 84 transmission and distribution projects across eight states. The projects are expected to add approximately 2.5 gigawatts (GW) of grid capacity to help mitigate outages and create greater grid resilience. The TVA award is for approximately $581 million in total, including $250 million in federal funding and about $331 million in applicant cost-share funding.
As part of the Resilience Amplified: Multi-Market Grid Interconnection Initiative funding award under the Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) project, the investments will help ensure 2.58 million families and businesses have access to the affordable, reliable, and secure power they need. The project is estimated to support about 800 jobs.
“Since day one, President Trump has recognized that years of misguided energy policies under the previous administration left our bulk power system less robust than it should be,” said U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy James P. Danly . “America is blessed with an abundance of natural resources and some of the most advanced technology in the world, but we must have the generation and transmission infrastructure necessary to support our rapidly growing economy and its electricity needs. These investments with TVA will help reduce congestion, improve efficiency, and make better use of our existing transmission system to lower costs for ratepayers while delivering affordable, reliable, and secure energy essential to American prosperity.”
“America's electric grid cannot become a roadblock to economic growth,” said Office of Electricity (OE) Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza . “By bringing TVA and local utilities together, we're helping reduce costly outages and deliver more power where it's needed. That means fewer disruptions for families, more opportunities for businesses, and a stronger foundation for American jobs.”
The award builds on DOE's selection of TVA for the Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades (SPARK) program . Together, the GRIP and SPARK projects for TVA represent nearly $741 million in planned grid investment, including approximately $329.8 million in federal support, and are expected to add more than 4,300 MW of additional grid capacity.
Under SPARK, TVA plans to upgrade about 125 miles of existing transmission lines across Tennessee, Alabama, and North Carolina using advanced conductors and grid-management technology. The $159.7 million project is expected to add approximately 1,900 MW of transmission capacity and reduce congestion.
Final federal funding, project scope, schedules, and other award conditions remain subject to executed DOE agreements and applicable environmental, permitting, regulatory, and Tribal reviews.

DOE’s Early Career Research Program (ECRP) Supports the Next Generation of American Scientific Leadership Across Universities, National Laboratories, and User Facilities.
Energy.gov
October 8, 2026
Estimated Read Time min
WASHINGTON— The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Science today announced the selection of 67 early career scientists to receive a combined $96 million through the 2026 Early Career Research Program (ECRP). Today’s announcement advances President Trump’s Executive Order Restoring Gold Standard Science by supporting exceptional researchers pursuing rigorous, mission-driven research in areas critical to America’s scientific and technological leadership, including Super Intelligence (SI), fusion energy, and quantum science.
“Groundbreaking science begins with empowering extraordinary people,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Dr. Darío Gil. “These 67 early career researchers represent the very best of American ingenuity. DOE is proud to invest in their vision as they push the boundaries of knowledge and cement U.S. leadership in the technologies that will define our century.”
The 2026 Early Career Research Program (ECRP) selectees represent 39 universities, 11 DOE National Laboratories and Office of Science User Facilities, and 26 states. By investing in exceptional researchers at a pivotal stage in their careers, ECRP empowers the next generation of STEM leaders to pursue bold, innovative research that drives DOE’s mission and ensures America continues to lead the world in science and innovation. Since its inception in 2010, the program has made 1,238 awards, including 797 to university researchers and 441 to DOE National Laboratory researchers.
Awards to scientists at institutions of higher education are approximately $875,000 over five years, while awards to scientists at DOE National Laboratories or Office of Science User Facilities are approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
Information about the 67 selectees and their research projects is available on the Office of Science Awards page .
Profiles of previous award recipients, including information about how the program helped advance their research and careers, are available on the Early Career Program profiles page .
Selection for award negotiations is not a commitment by DOE to issue an award or provide funding. Before funding is issued, DOE and the applicants will undergo a negotiation process, and DOE may cancel negotiations and rescind the selection for any reason during that time.

Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
Today in Energy
Skip to page content
In-brief analysis
October 9, 2026
Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
Data source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, U.S. Energy Atlas map of hurricanes, cyclones, and typhoons ; National Weather Service’s National Hurricane Center Note: LNG=liquefied natural gas
As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructure. Hurricane Isaias is the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season and will be the largest storm system to make landfall in the region since Hurricane Helene in September 2024.
Hurricane Isaias’s forecasted path toward the Gulf Coast has already impacted crude oil and natural gas production in the region. The Marine Minerals Administration reports that as of Thursday, October 8, 130 production platforms and rigs have been evacuated or moved resulting in production shut-ins of about 1.3 million barrels per day of crude oil and 1.1 billion million cubic feet per day of natural gas. The U.S. Gulf Coast is home to a large portion of the U.S. refining fleet, and the impacts from Hurricane Isaias could affect refinery operations .

windows.text: Hurricane Isaias’s forecasted path toward the Gulf Coast has already impacted crude oil and natural gas production in the region. The Marine Minerals Administration reports that as of Thursday, October 8, 130 production platforms and rigs have been evacuated or moved resulting in production shut-ins of about 1.3 million barrels per day of crude oil and 1.1 billion million cubic feet per day of natural gas. The U.S. Gulf Coast is home to a large portion of the U.S. refining fleet, and the impacts from Hurricane Isaias could affect refinery operations .
